Author: leo lu
Body HTML:
Geze EMD F-9/10 Technical Manual & Connection Guide

This document provides technical details, connection instructions, and parameter settings for the Geze EMD F-9/10 automatic door drive systems.

Connection Overview

Note: In 2-leaf assemblies, the outer contractor can be connected to the moving leaf control or to the fixed leaf control.
  • In selection, the moving leaf opens and, if switched on, the fixed leaf follows.
  • In selection, the output of the authorized contractor is closed (24 V applied at input).

Tamper Function

The tamper function can be parameterized for Input SI1 or SI2. The tamper contact is usually closed (24 V applied).

  • Parameter t2: Applied at input. The tamper function can be parameterized for Input SI1 or SI2.

Accessories

  • Profile half-cylinder: Mat. No. 090044 (Includes switch housing)
  • Profile half-cylinder: Mat. No. 121094 (Additional contact)
  • Remote control: Mat. No. 122003
  • Ceiling integration kit: Mat. No. 099583
  • Rain cover: Mat. No. 099550

Input 51 (Inner Contractor)

The input 51 is active in 2L (2-leaf) and 1L (1-leaf) modes.

  • In 2-leaf assemblies, the inner contractor can be connected to the moving leaf control or to the fixed leaf control.
  • In selection, the moving leaf opens and, if switched on, the fixed leaf follows.
  • In selection, the output of the inner contractor is closed (24 V applied at input 51).
  • The sensor for monitoring closing can also be used as an inner contractor. To this end, set the parameter accordingly.
  • Parameter t1: Can be used to set an activation delay for input 51. This time is added to the activation delay set with parameter t2.

Input 52 (Outer Contractor)

The input 52 is active in 2L mode only.

  • In 2-leaf assemblies, the outer contractor can be connected to the moving leaf control or to the fixed leaf control.
  • In selection, the moving leaf opens and, if switched on, the fixed leaf also opens.
  • In selection, the output of the outer contractor is closed (24 V applied at input 52).
  • The sensor for monitoring closing can also be used as an outer contractor. To this end, set the parameter accordingly.
  • Parameter t3: Can be used to set an activation delay for input 52. This time is added to the activation delay set with parameter t2.

Movement Detectors (GC 302)

Refer to connection diagrams WC922, WC923, WC924.

The GC 302 is a directionally sensitive radar (microwave) motion detector.

  • Installation: Follow the installation instructions provided with the device (Mat. No. 132002).
  • Configuration: According to EN 16005.
  • Note: Remote control does not work if the hood is fitted (IR not visible).

Stop Function

The stop function is controlled via a pushbutton.

  • In 2-leaf assemblies, the door leaf stops (both leaves in 2-leaf assemblies) and remains stopped as long as the input is active.
  • The stop button can be connected to the moving leaf control or to the fixed leaf control.
  • Set Parameter 42 accordingly.

Important Safety Note

Stop must be connected to SI2 for personal protection in accordance with DIN 18650.

To monitor the entrance, a 8.2 kΩ terminating resistor must be connected and Parameter b1 must be set to 02.

Switching Contact Function

This function allows for step-by-step control (Open/Close).

  • Set Parameter b0 or b1 accordingly.
  • In activation, the scanner output is closed (24 V is applied to input SI1 or SI2).
  • The first momentary contact opens the door, the next one closes the door.
  • With Parameter b0(b1) = 04: The door automatically closes at the end of the hold open time, if it has not been closed beforehand using the pushbutton.
2-Leaf Operations: If the pushbutton is connected to the fixed leaf control, both door leaves open and close on selection of the momentary contact function, even if the fixed leaf control is switched off (bed opening / fully open).

Geze DPS Program Switch

 Geze EMD F-Technical Manual: Connections & Configuration

Program Switches

The Geze EMD-F supports various program switches for controlling door operating modes. The system distinguishes between internal and external program switches.

Supported Switch Types

  • DPS (Display Program Switch): Used for commissioning and service. Part No. 115525 (GC 338).
  • MPS (Mechanical Program Switch): Standard mechanical switch for mode selection.
  • TPS (Key Program Switch): Key-operated switch for secure mode selection.
  • MPS-ST: Mechanical program switch for specific configurations.

Control Priorities

The system inputs prioritize signals in the following order:

  1. Input NA (Night/Locked) takes precedence over inputs NA, LS, AU, and DO.
  2. If DPS is applied to the input, it overrides other mechanical switches.

Note: If the DPS is used, the code cannot be changed via the TPS. Configuration changes via TPS are only possible if no signal is queued at the NA, LS, AU, and DO inputs.

Operating Modes & Input Signals

The drive switches to specific operating modes when a 24 V signal is applied to the corresponding input terminals (KL 1).

Operating Mode Input Mappings
Signal Input Description
NA Night (Locked) - High Priority
LS Shop Closing / Exit Only
AU Automatic Mode
DO Permanently Open (Dauerauf)

Output Configuration (PA1 & PA2)

The controller provides two programmable outputs for status signaling and external system integration.

PA1 Output

PA1 is a floating relay contact. It is typically used for switching voltage or current.

  • Rating: Max. 24 V AC/DC, 1 A
  • Default Function: Configurable via Parameter A1 (e.g., Door status).

PA2 Output

PA2 is a transistor output (Active Low/High depending on config).

  • Rating: 24 V DC / 0.2 A
  • Default Function: Configurable via Parameter A2.
  • Example: Set Parameter A2 to 01 for specific fault indication or status reporting.

Fault Indication

If a system fault occurs, the corresponding error number is displayed on the DPS or TPS. Example configuration:

  • Set Parameter A2 to 01 for Fault Indication output.
  • Output switches after 3 sec (configurable via control detects).

Accessories

Compatible accessories for the Geze EMD F system:

  • Surface Mount Socket (Single): GC 306, Part No. 100010
  • Display Program Switch (Geze DPS): GC 338, Part No. 115525
  • Profile Half Cylinder: Part No. 090176
  • Fan for Motor Cooling: Configurable via output parameters (e.g., A2 = 05 to drive a fan).

Display & Troubleshooting

Switching Master/Slave Operation

To toggle between Master (1-leaf) and Slave (2-leaf) display modes:

  1. Simultaneously press keys on the DPS.
  2. The DPS display indicates the mode: 1 (Master) or 2 (Slave).

In the event of an error, the error code is displayed (see DPS error messages).

Author: leo lu
Body HTML:
GEZE EMD-F Installation Manual - Door Opener & Smoke Switch Control

This document details the connection procedures for door openers and smoke switch controls (RSZ 6) for the GEZE EMD-F and TSA 160 systems. Please ensure all safety precautions are followed during installation.

Door Opener Connections

Proper wiring of the door opener is critical for correct operation of the active and passive leaves.

  • Active Leaf: Connect the door opener of the active leaf to the active leaf controller connection terminal.
  • Passive (Fixed) Leaf: Connect the door opener of the fixed leaf to the fixed leaf controller connection terminal.

Configuration Parameters

  • Use the designated Parameter to set the type of door opener.
  • Activation Duration: Activation of the door opener is limited to a specific time (typically 4 seconds).
  • Motor Locks: If a motor lock without a feedback signal is used, an activation delay must be set via parameter. This provides the motor lock sufficient time for unlocking before the drive engages.
  • Lock Type Selection: Use exit door openers, magnetic clamps, or 24 V DC motor locks only.
Important: Do not use working current (fail-secure) door openers. Ensure only 24 V DC compatible locks are used.

Electrical Wiring & Terminals

Diode Protection

Connect a free-wheeling diode to the door opener when using DC supply voltage to prevent voltage spikes that could damage the controller.

Input Signals & Logic

  • Locked Door Logic: The input signal blocks the drive selection if the door is locked.
  • Active State Behavior: If the input becomes active while the door is open, the door reverses direction and remains open.
  • Use the appropriate parameter to configure the type of lock signal (inverted or standard).

Terminal Overview

Standard Connection Terminals
Terminal Type Description
TO / GND / 24V Door Opener Power and Control
Input / Output Control Signals (Lock Status, Feedback)

Smoke Switch Control (RSZ 6)

The smoke switch control unit is a critical safety component. For a 2-leaf drive system, the smoke switch control must be connected to the same controller as the drive's reset button.

Installation Requirements

  • Follow the specific installation instructions provided with the smoke switch control unit.
  • The control unit loads the smoke control central with approximately 80 mA.
  • The smoke switch control central is connected to the printed circuit board (PCB) of the TSA 160 / EMD-F.

Emergency Behavior (Fire/Power Failure)

In the event of a fire alarm or power failure:

  1. The door opener and motor are immediately disconnected from the control.
  2. The door closes automatically by means of the spring force.
  3. For 2-leaf doors, both leaves will close.
  4. Note: The closing speed in this mode cannot be adjusted; it is determined by the spring force.

Connection Logic

Drive 1 (Active Leaf) and Drive 2 (Passive Leaf) must be wired such that the smoke switch interrupts the circuit effectively on both.

  • Reset Button: Must be connected to the reset contact.
  • Status Monitoring: The closed position of the fixed leaf is monitored with a reed switch. If the fixed leaf is not closed, the system may prevent the active leaf from locking or operating correctly.

Body HTML:
GEZE EMD F Technical Manual & Connection Guide
GEZE EMD-F Processor

Overview

This document provides technical details, connection diagrams, and function descriptions for the GEZE EMD F,and EMD Invers door drive systems. These systems are designed for reliable automatic door operation with specific modes for Low Energy and Servo functionality.

Connection Diagram

The system supports various connection configurations including SIS, SIS E, and SIS M. Proper wiring of the connection terminals is essential for safe operation.

Key Components

  • Control SIS: Connection terminals SIS 1, SIS 2, SIS 3.
  • GND: Ground connection points.
  • Inputs: KA, KB, KI signal inputs for activation.
  • Power Supply: Mains connection.

Electrical Data

Parameter Value
Power Supply 230 V AC, 50/60 Hz
Power Consumption 230 W
External Consumer Output 24 V DC (approx. 750-800 mA)

Low Energy Function

The drives EMD, EMD-F, and EMD Invers can be configured as Low Energy drives by adjusting the relevant parameters.

Safety & Limits

  • The kinetic energy in the door leaf must be limited to 1.69 J.
  • The static force on the main closing edge must be smaller than 67 N.
  • To achieve this, the opening speed (vo) and closing speed (vc) must be set according to the characteristic display field based on leaf mass and width.
  • Safety sensors are generally not required in Low Energy mode if these limits are met.

Parameter Adjustments

Hold-open time: The adjustment range for the hold-open time parameter is typically 0 to 60 seconds.

Servo Function

Drives EMD F and EMD Invers can be set as servo drives. This mode facilitates manual operation with motor assistance.

Operation Characteristics

  • In servo operation, the drive operates with force support, effectively compensating for the spring force.
  • The door can be easily opened or closed manually by the user.
  • The drive does not open automatically in this mode unless triggered.

Activation

The servo function is initiated by:

  • Activating inputs KI, KA, KB.
  • Changing settings to DO (Automatic) mode.
  • Manual opening of the door.

Note: If no activation signal is applied and the operating mode is not set to Automatic, the door will close automatically after the set hold-open time has expired.

Leaf Dimension & Weight

The operational limits of the drive depend on the leaf width and weight. Consult the characteristic field diagram for precise settings.

  • Leaf Width Range: Typically 0.50 m to 1.60 m.
  • Max Weight: Up to approximately 230 kg (dependent on width).
  • Example: A leaf width of 1.25 m may support approximately 100 kg.

GEZE EMD-F Commissioning and Service Instructions | Technical Manual
Geze DPS Program Switch

Table of Contents

  • 1. General Information
  • 2. Putting into Service: Single Leaf
  • 3. Putting into Service: Two Leaf
  • 4. Learning Process & Parameters
  • 5. Troubleshooting & Errors

1. General Information

The DPS (Display Programme Switch) is required for commissioning and service operations.

  • Changing drive parameters
  • "Teaching" (adapting) the drive to the door system
  • Diagnosis and troubleshooting

Note: Buttons are not pressed for 1 minute in service mode, the system automatically switches back to operational mode.

In service mode, the door remains in the current type of operation (not if teach is activated).

2. Putting into Service: Single Leaf

The putting into service process involves checking installation and setting parameters for your GEZE EMD. Refer to the standard single leaf commissioning procedure:

  1. Ensure mechanical assembly is completed.
  2. Verify electrical installation.
  3. Ensure all sensors are correctly programmed and aligned.

Important: Under parameter 10.6, do not change settings arbitrarily. Ensure the leaf type matches the drive configuration (Lead/Fixed leaf).

3. Putting into Service: Two Leaf

Commissioning a two-leaf GEZE EMD system requires specific steps to ensure coordination between leaves.

Pre-requisites:

  • 10.1 Assembly is fully completed.
  • 10.2 Electrical installation is completed (Power and Control lines).
  • 10.3 Sensors are correctly programmed and aligned.
  • 10.4 Set the internal program switches of both drives to "0" (or required standard setting).

Step-by-Step Procedure:

  1. Switch off the fixed leaf control: Disconnect the 24V DC plug.
  2. If necessary, completely close the fixed leaf manually.
  3. Remove any existing programme switch (TPS) and connect the DPS to the moving leaf control.
  4. Switch on the moving leaf control:
    • For DSA-I (Inverse) drives, Error 28 may be displayed at the DPS. This is standard during initial setup.
    • Press the RESET button on the controller if required.

4. Learning Process & Parameters

The drive must "learn" the physical characteristics of the door.

Initiating the Teach-In:

The drive "learning" process is started with the OK button on the DPS.

The control learns the following parameters automatically:

  • Start position
  • Closed position
  • Open position
  • Wall blanking of the Open presence sensor
  • Spring force adjustments

During the process, the display will show the motor current required to hold open the door. If an error occurs, the learning is cancelled with message !4.

Finishing Moving Leaf Settings:

After the learning run:

  • Switch to use Service Mode.
  • Set dC1 (initially configured as 1-leaf drive).
  • Configure Door Type settings:
    • Close presence sensor
    • Open safety sensor
    • Testing safety sensors
    • Door opener / Lock signal
    • If necessary, set parameters for motor-driven lock.

Fixed Leaf Configuration:

  1. Disconnect connection to moving leaf control.
  2. Connect DPS to the fixed leaf control.
  3. Switch on the fixed leaf control.
  4. Press the DSA-I Reset button (if applicable).
  5. Perform "Teach-in" for the fixed leaf similar to the moving leaf.

5. Re-Teaching and Diagnostics

Anytime a mechanical change occurs, the drive must be "re-taught".

Re-Teaching Both Drives:

If both drives have already been in operation, they can be re-taught together ("Retaining" process):

  1. If necessary, remove TPS at fixed leaf control and connect DPS.
  2. Switch to Service Mode.
  3. Confirm "Teach" command.
  4. Monitor the DPS for the sequence: Start → Closed → Open.

Common Display Codes:

  • !4: Learning cancelled / Error.
  • 28: DSA-I specific code (often requires Reset).
  • E* codes: Check sensor connections.

Author: leo lu
Body HTML:
GEZE EMD-F 21-22 Instruction Manual | Installation & Configuration

GEZE EMD-F Swing Door Drive

General Settings

Configure the movement parameters for the GEZE EMD-F door drive.

Opening Speed
Adjusts the speed at which the door opens. Range: 0-100%.
Closing Speed
Adjusts the speed at which the door closes. Range: 0-100%.
Latching Action
Speed in the last few degrees of closing (closed position) to ensure the door latches reliably.
Hold Open Time
The duration the door remains open before starting to close automatically. Adjustable.
Dynamic Hold Open Extension
Automatically extends the hold open time based on traffic volume or usage.

Door Configuration

Setup for single or double leaf door systems, including standard GEZE EMD F components.

  • Moving Leaf / Fixed Leaf: Configuration for active and passive leaves in double-door systems.
  • Door Coordination: Settings for 1-leaf moving leaf without mechanical door coordination device.
  • Single Action Door: Basic setup for standard swing doors.

Operating Modes

The system supports various operating modes selectable via the Program Switch (DPS).

Mode Description
Automatic (Day) Door opens automatically on activation and closes after the hold open time.
Night Door is locked (if electromechanical lock is present) and sensors are disabled. Access via authorized key switch only.
Shop Door functions automatically but with reduced opening width or altered timings.
Off Drive motor is deactivated. Door behaves like a manual door closer.
Exit Only One-way traffic; external sensors are disabled.

Functions

Push and Go
If the door is pushed manually, the drive detects the movement and completes the opening cycle automatically.
Power Assist / Servo
Reduces the manual force required to open the door.
Low Energy Operation
Restricts kinetic energy for safety compliance (DIN 18650 / EN 16005) without safety sensors in some applications.
Backcheck
Braking action during opening to prevent the door from slamming into a wall (Wind Stop function).

Input & Output Signals

Configuration of programmable inputs and outputs for integration with building management systems.

Programmable Inputs

  • Input SIS/SIO: Safety sensors (Opening/Closing side).
  • KB: Contact activation.
  • Input 1 / Input 2: Configurable for various triggers (e.g., Interlock, Fire Alarm).

Programmable Outputs

  • Door Open: Signal when door is in open position.
  • Fault/Alarm: Signal when an error is detected.
  • Locked/Unlocked: Feedback on locking status.
  • Gong: Activation signal for external chime.

Error Handling & Display

The control unit features a display for status and error codes.

Tip: Error messages can be acknowledged or cleared from the memory locally or via the service terminal (ST 220).
  • Display Orientation: Can be rotated 180° for easier reading depending on mounting.
  • Service Interval: Prompts for maintenance after a set number of cycles.
  • Error Memory: Stores past errors for diagnostics. Can be deleted via the menu.

Title: GEZE EMD-F Troubleshooting: Error Codes & Solutions Guide
Author: leo lu
Body HTML:
GEZE EMD-F Error Codes & Troubleshooting Guide

Geze DPS Program Switch

Overview

This guide provides a detailed list of error codes, causes, and solutions for the GEZE EMD-F automatic door system. The errors are indicated on the display switch or the internal service display.

Note: DCU1, DCU1-2, DCU1-2M connection diagrams and specific controller behaviors are referenced below.

Error Codes List

Error Code Description / Cause
01 Control is defective.
02 / 22 Mains power supply failure.
03 / 27 Smoke detector active.
04 Rotary transducer signal is faulty.
05 Motor current too large.
06 Motor defective.
09 Closing safety sensor test faulty or activation longer than minimum.
0A Inconsistent condition at input SIS or SIS cable break.
0B No communication between control and program switch.
0C Door opener does not unblock (Lock stuck).
0D Door opener does not trigger (Unlock trigger failed).
0F Closing safety sensor test faulty or activation longer than minimum.
13 / 14 Lever arm or rod not fixed.

Author: leo lu
Body HTML:
DORMA ES 200 / Easy / 2D User Manual - Safety, Installation & Maintenance

ES200 Sliding Door Operator

Table of Contents

  • For Your Safety
  • Intended Application
  • Installation & Mounting
  • Commissioning
  • Operation & Briefing
  • Maintenance, Care & Wear
  • Technical Data
  • Recycling & Disposal

For Your Safety

This documentation contains important information regarding the mounting and the safe operation of the door system. Please read these instructions carefully before using the dorma es 200, the ES 200 Easy, or the ES 200-2D.

Important: It is important for your personal safety to abide by all enclosed instructions. An incorrectly performed installation might cause serious injuries.

Using control elements, making adjustments or performing procedures that are not described in this documentation might cause electric shocks, danger caused by electric voltage/current and/or danger due to mechanical incidents.

Please keep these documents for further reference and hand them over to the person in charge in case the system is transferred to another party.

Explanation of Symbols

WARNING: This symbol underlines important information that may facilitate your work. It warns you of possible system damage and explains how to avoid this damage. It indicates dangers that might cause personal or material damage or even kill people.

Safety Instructions

  • Work on electrical equipment may only be performed by properly qualified staff (electricians).
  • Do not allow children to play with the dormakaba es 200, the ES 200 Easy, the ES 200-2D or its adjustment and control devices.
  • Keep remote controls out of reach of children.
  • Never stick metal objects into the openings of the ES 200, the ES 200 Easy or the ES 200-2D; otherwise you might sustain an electric shock.
  • If the unit is mounted onto a metal door leaf, you have to earth (ground) the door leaf properly.
  • Glass door leaves have to be made of safety glass.

Limitation of Liability

The ES 200, the ES 200 Easy and the ES 200-2D may only be used according to its specified intended application. DORMA GmbH + Co. KG will not accept any liability for damage resulting from unauthorised modifications. Furthermore, components/accessories that have not been approved by DORMA are exempted from liability.

Intended Application

  • ES 200 Easy: Designed to open and close interior sliding doors with an admissible door panel weight up to 1 x 100 kg or 2 x 85 kg. Neither suitable for escape routes, fire/smoke doors, nor exterior doors.
  • es200: Designed to open and close interior sliding doors with an admissible door panel weight up to 1 x 200 kg or 2 x 160 kg. Neither suitable for escape routes, fire/smoke doors, nor exterior doors.
  • ES 200-2D: Designed to open and close interior sliding doors with an admissible door panel weight up to 1 x 150 kg or 2 x 130 kg. Suitable for application in escape routes. Not suitable for fire/smoke doors or exterior doors. The maximum cable length for external components must not exceed 30 m.

Safety During Mounting

  • The working area has to be secured against unauthorised access from other people. Falling items or tools might cause injuries.
  • The system must be secured against water and other liquids.
  • The mounting equipment (screws, wall plugs) must be adequate with regard to the structural conditions (steel structure, wood, concrete etc.).
  • Structural or local conditions might suggest a different approach than described in the examples.
  • Following installation, the settings and proper function of the unit and safety equipment have to be checked.
  • Only specially qualified staff may open the power supply housing.
  • Disconnect from power supply (de-energise the system) before removing the cover of the power supply housing. Remove mains plug or switch off fuse.
  • Always pull at the plug and never at the cable when unplugging the power supply.

Safety During Commissioning

  • The protective earth conductor has to be connected.
  • The safety sensors are to be connected (see commissioning instructions).
  • The operator and the active panels must be properly linked.
  • The end stops must be adjusted so that the sliding panels meet the end stops when the system is adjusted to its maximum opening width.
  • The sealing profiles of the active panels and the passive panels must not collide while the door is closed.
  • Separately supplied components such as the program switch, EMERGENCY OFF pushbutton, and activators (radar motion detectors, NIGHT-/BANK key switches) have to be mounted and connected.
  • Ensure that the door leaves run smoothly.
  • The rechargeable battery pack has been installed (optional).

Inspection and System Approval

Before the first commissioning and depending on requirements (at least once a year), the system must be inspected by a properly qualified technician and serviced if required.

A person trained by DORMA has to perform the inspection and approve the system with the aid of the inspection book. The results have to be documented in accordance with DIN 18650-2, and the facility operator has to keep these documents for at least one year.

Operation & Briefing

Briefing

Following the adjustment, commissioning, and functional testing of the door system, the operating instructions have to be handed over to the facility operator and a briefing has to be made.

Behaviour During Varying Weather Conditions

The safety sensors (infrared light curtains) are designed to safeguard the passage area. When adjusting sensitivity, the protection of people always has top priority.

Changing climatic conditions (rain, snow), flying leaves, or direct sunlight (reflected by floors) may accidentally trigger sensors. If triggered, the door may remain open for up to one minute – a standard procedure to protect users.

Danger Spots at Closing Edges

Automatic doors might cause hazards by crushing, shearing, hitting, and drawing-in at the different closing edges (Main closing edge, Secondary closing edge).

Residual Risk

Depending on structural conditions, door version, and safety equipment, residual risks such as crushing and hitting (with limited force) cannot be completely excluded.

Maintenance, Care & Wear

Maintenance & Cleaning

WARNING: The system has to be de-energised (disconnected from power supply) before performing any kind of maintenance work or cleaning. Remove the power plug or switch off the fuse.
  • Clean with a damp cloth and standard commercial detergents.
  • Do not use scouring agents as they might damage the surface finish.
  • Ensure no water or liquids drop on or into the unit.
  • Never stick metal objects into openings.

Wear Parts Schedule

The following wear parts must be checked in regular intervals and replaced if required to ensure smooth function. Only use original spare parts.

Component Maintenance Interval
Track rollers Every 2 years
Rubber end stops At every service check
Track rail Every 5 years
Toothed belt Every 1,000,000 opening/closing cycles
Floor guides At every service check
Brushes (optional) Clean/Check regularly

Important Technical Data & Standards

  • Power supply: 230 V
  • Fuse (by others): 16 A
  • Operating noise: < 70 dB(A)
  • Admissible humidity: 93% relative humidity, non-condensing
  • Admissible temperature: -20°C to +60°C

Standards, Laws, Codes and Regulations

The latest versions of common and country-specific standards (e.g., DIN 18650) must be observed.

During planning, the manufacturer (installer) and the commissioner/facility operator must perform an individual risk assessment. Refer to the DORMA website for risk assessment forms.

Recycling and Disposal

Both the ES 200 series units and their packing mainly consist of recyclable raw material.

The appliances and accessories must not be disposed of as domestic waste.

Please ensure that the old appliance and accessories are properly disposed of in accordance with prevailing national statutory provisions.

Title: DORMA ES 200 Easy / 2D Installation & Adjustment Manual
Author: leo lu
Body HTML:

DORMA ES 200 Easy / ES 200-2D Automatic Door Installation Manual & Guide

1. Safety & Electrical Requirements

Important: Work on electrical equipment may only be performed by properly qualified electricians.
  • Power Supply: On site with 16 A fuse protection.
  • Cabling: Connecting cable must be double insulated (e.g., NYM). Do not use flat webbed house wires.
  • Accessories: The instructions accompanying the accessories must be strictly observed.

2. Fixing & Installation Preparations

Before beginning the installation of the Dorma ES 200 Easy, verify your fixing method and dimensions.

Installation Types

  • Wall Fixing: Direct wall installation.
  • Corridor Installation: Using aluminium girder.

Track Rail Preparation

  1. Fix the track rail.
  2. Assemble the roller carriers and fix them in place.
  3. Prepare mounting and aluminium girder for the light barrier cable.

3. Drive Unit & Belt Assembly

Mini Drive Unit & Pulley

  1. Installation of Mini Drive Unit and pulley (locking device).
  2. Fix and adjust the Mini Drive unit.
  3. Screw down the pulley (locking device).

Toothed Belt Installation

  1. Install toothed belt, cover holder, and accessories.
  2. Trimming: Trim and secure the toothed belt manually.
  3. Tensioning: Tighten screw of clamping device until bolt head and end of cover are aligned.
  4. Screw down pulley (locking device) tightly.

Belt Adjustment

If the toothed belt rubs excessively against the bottom pulley flange causing noise, it requires readjustment:

  1. Loosen the right fixing screw of the pulley (locking device).
  2. Wind in the adjustment screw until the belt runs centrally again.
  3. Tighten the right fixing screw of the pulley.

4. Adjustments & Fine-Tuning

Locking Device (Optional)

Perform adjustment of the locking device if equipped.

Closing Sliding Panels

  1. Unscrew cage.
  2. Insert lock bolt.
  3. Adjust cage and secure it.

Covers & Hinge Profiles

  • Internal Cover: Insert hinge profiles into internal cover. Break edges of internal cover according to stipulated dimensions to ensure proper fixing of end plates.
  • Earth Grounding: Use earthing cable to ground the inner cover.
  • Fixing: Insert hinge profile into inner cover and install manually into mounting girder, starting in the middle. Open and fix the inner cover.
  • End Plates: Trim end plates as needed.

Connect unit to power supply (supplied by others) and perform a test run.

5. Mounting Instructions

General Mounting

Fix mounting girder with at least 6 screws. Screws must be positioned equally along the length of the girder.

Wall Fixing

Requirements vary by surface material:

  • Masonry: Heavy-duty plugs must be used (supplied by others).
    • Mark and drill holes.
    • Insert plugs.
    • Shim mounting plate as appropriate and fix with countersunk screws.
  • Steel:
    • Mark, drill, and tap the holes.
    • Shim mounting plate as appropriate and fix with countersunk screws.

Corridor Fixing

  • Masonry: Mark and drill holes, insert heavy-duty plugs.
  • Steel: Mark holes, drill to 5mm diameter, and tap M6 threads.
  • Assembly: Insert square nuts into profile slots. Mount aluminium girder with ES profile bolted in place. Align and screw down tight.

Side Screens & Light Barriers

  • Wall Brackets: Fix U-section profiles according to sketch dimensions. Mark, drill, insert plugs, align brackets, and screw down tight. Insert side screens and fix.
  • Floor Guide: Screw down floor guide rail to building or side screen.
  • Light Barriers: Mount the cable into the installation. Use shrinkdown plastic tubing in the mounting girder area for protection. Insert light barriers into profile slots and screw down profiles.

6. Sliding Panels & Door Alignment

Panel Assembly

Assemble the sliding panels for the Dorma ES200 and prepare for adjustment.

Clearance & Parallelism

  • Floor Clearance: Set floor or floor guide clearance at the sliding panel to 6 mm.
    • Relax brackets of main and secondary closing edge.
    • Adjust height with hexagon nut.
    • Screw down tight.
  • Parallelism: Open door to check centre seals are parallel with side screens. Close door and open slightly to check gap consistency over entire height.

Derailment Guard

Release derailment guard of roller carriers and adjust:

  1. Undo bolts in diagonal oblong holes of carriers.
  2. Adjust derailment guard to a clearance of 0.5 mm with respect to track rail and mounting girder.
  3. Check for smooth running and re-tighten bolts.

End Stops & Opening Width

  1. Insert end stops.
  2. Move both sliding panels manually to full opening width and secure.
  3. Move end buffers to meet sliding panels and screw down tight.

Centre Alignment (AM vs SK)

Viewed from inside, determine the centre point of the door set (AM).

  1. Relax connection between carrier and toothed belt on the left sliding panel.
  2. Move both sliding panels manually until the closing edge (SK) coincides with the door set centre (AM).
  3. Re-tighten connection.
  4. Correction: For major discrepancies, move the toothed belt one or more tooth pitches along.

7. Final Check Up

  • Derailment guard / counter roller adjusted correctly (0.5 mm)?
  • Door panels run smoothly with no grinding noise?
  • Electromechanical locking adjusted correctly (> 1mm)?
  • All shortened wires provided with end splices?
  • All connectors plugged in?
  • All cables fixed? No obstacles within the driving phase?
  • (Only for ES 200 with "Emergency opening function") Serial connection with "internal sensor" performed?

Title: Record 16 STA / 16 STA-UL Installation & Safety Manual
Author: leo lu
Body HTML:
2. General Remarks

This manual is intended for qualified, trained, and authorised installers of the record 16 STA / record 16 STA-UL pedestrian sliding door operator.

The manual describes the correct installation and commissioning procedure.

The product is subject to technical modification. There can therefore be differences between the product and the manual.

2.1 Symbols

Various symbols are used in this manual for simplification:

Note: Especially useful details concerning installation.
Caution: Special details indispensable for satisfactory operation of the system.
Danger: Details for the prevention of damage to persons and material.

3. Safety Instructions

The record 16 STA / record 16 STA-UL pedestrian sliding door operator has been constructed in accordance with the latest state of the art and the recognised technical safety regulations, including limiting of forces and speeds. Nevertheless, danger can arise for the user if not used as intended.

Installation, maintenance, and repairs to the record 16 STA / record 16 STA-UL pedestrian sliding door operator must only be performed by qualified, trained, and authorised personnel (technicians).

3.1 Use for the intended purpose

The record 16 STA / record 16 STA-UL pedestrian sliding door operator is designed exclusively for normal service with automatic pedestrian sliding doors and must be installed indoors.

Any other application or use beyond this purpose is not considered to be the use for the intended purpose. The manufacturer bears no liability for any resulting damage; the installer and/or end user alone shall bear the responsibility.

Use for the intended purpose also includes observation of the operating conditions specified by the manufacturer, in addition to regular care, maintenance, and repair.

Unauthorised modifications to the pedestrian sliding door operator and/or its installation exclude all liability of the manufacturer for resulting damage.

3.2 General safety and accident prevention regulations

  • No safety devices (sensors) may be dismantled or placed out of service.
  • No persons or objects must be present in the opening area/path of the sliding door, in order to avoid crushing and cutting.
  • The automatic pedestrian sliding door operator is not intended to be disconnected from the mains at night!

3.3 Safety and accident prevention instruction for installations in compliance with UL325

Before applying the mains voltage to the power supply, the installer has to ensure that the mains voltage selector switch on the power supply NET 16-UL is switched to the correct position (115V / 230V).

The mains power connection has to be done via the mains power cord provided with the pedestrian sliding door operator. Proper grounding has to be applied. Only permanent wiring is allowed with this pedestrian sliding door operator.

Wherever 230V only is mentioned throughout this manual, either 115V or 230V is meant, according to the applied mains voltage in the country it is to be installed.

If any electrical unit (photoelectric sensor, radar, control unit, control panel, etc.) is not mounted within the existing construction of the automatic sliding door installation (e.g., on an adjacent wall), the installer shall protect the cabling from any damage and shall prevent any stress on their connections by proper means. The local installation codes have always to be followed.

WARNING: To avoid risk of electric shock, disconnect mains power (115 / 230V) before servicing.

The delivered red label with the above text has to be placed within the cover above the NET 16-UL module in such a manner that it be seen as soon as the cover is opened.
DANGER: The edges of the cut profiles may be sharp. Be careful so as to avoid injury.
WARNING: The installer shall minimize the sharp edges at each profile, especially at the end of the profiles, where the side covers are placed.
NOTE: The installer must visually inspect the pedestrian sliding door operator for sharp edges and eliminate them before completing the installation.
WARNING: Caution, the pedestrian sliding door operator contains moving parts. Be careful after having opened the cover.
WARNING: To reduce risk of injury to persons, use this operator only with sliding pedestrian doors for residential, commercial, or industrial use.
WARNING: Use copper conductors only for any wiring on the pedestrian sliding door operator installation.
WARNING: For continued protection against fire, replace any fuse only with the same type and rating.

If the pedestrian sliding door operator is used without a radar sensor to be opened, and a switch is used instead, the switch is to be installed in a location from which operation of the door can be observed by the person operating the switch.

The glazing material in both fixed and sliding panels of a sliding door shall comply with the requirements in the Safety Performance Specifications and Methods of Test within the standard ANSI Z97.1-1984 Safety Glazing Material Used in Buildings (chapter 29.5 of UL 325).

WARNING: The correct behaviour of the door according to the programmed parameters via the BDE must be verified during commissioning.

3.4 Final adjustments and tests on site for proper operation for compliance with UL325

  • Check that all tasks defined in chapter 8 "Commissioning and final work" have been carried out properly.
  • Check that the door may be opened manually without power applied to the unit.
  • Remove mains power supply and battery connection and check that the door may be opened manually with a force not greater than 222.4N (50 lbf). (Chapter 29.3.2 of UL 325)
  • Check that the door does not develop kinetic energy in excess of 9.49J (7 ft-lbf). (Chapter 29.4.1 of UL 325)
  • Check that the door does not require a force greater than 133.4N (30 lbf) applied in either direction to prevent the door from closing. (Chapter 29.4.1 of UL 325)
  • Check that one photoelectric sensor is installed at a height between 150 and 300mm.
  • Check with a white vertical surface (305 by 152mm) that the photoelectric sensor is working correctly at a total of 5 different locations including a distance of 25.4mm from each end. (Chapter 35.2 of UL 325)
  • Check that the mains power field wired connections are located inside the enclosure of the operator.

Title: Installation Instructions - Manual Record 16 STA / 16 STA-UL
Author: leo lu
Body HTML:
Installation Instructions - Manual Record 16 STA / 16 STA-UL

These instructions cover the installation processes for the Manual Record 16 STA and 16 STA-UL systems.

  • Start of installation with cladding profile: See section 7.1
  • Start of installation without cladding profile: See section 7.10

7.1 Start of Installation Using Cladding Profile

The exact dimensions are given on the general installation drawings or on separate drawings or diagrams.

7.2 Fixing the Cladding Profile P1307

7.2.1 Type of Installation: Self-Supporting

  • Fitting of cladding holder 016.000.005
  • Inserting cladding profile P1307
  • Fixing cladding profile to cladding holders with 4 self-tapping screws (contained in 016.006.000)

7.2.2 Type of Installation: Lintel Installation

  • Cut cladding profile to length
  • Drill fixing holes in cladding profile (Through holes 9 mm dia.)
  • Fit cladding profile exactly horizontally and vertically.

Note: At least four screws should be used for fixing. The cladding profile must lie flat. It is self-supporting up to 5.1 m (A = 2.5m) by using side screens.

7.3 Installation of Side Screens and/or Wall Connection Profile

Side Screens:

  • Mark centre of door on floor
  • Cut wall connection profile P1336 / P1357 to length (30 mm) or P1335 / P1356 (20 mm)
  • Align and fix profile
  • Align and fix floor profile P1315 (30 mm) or P1319 (20 mm)
  • Perform height levelling with hex. screw or socket-head hex. screw (contained in 016.121.000 for 20mm or 016.141.000 for 30mm)
  • When using a 20 mm profile system, an infill-profile 10 mm P1311 with tensioning blocks (016.000.007) must be used in the cladding profile P1307. Fixing of tensioning blocks with a 2 mm Allen key (contained in 016.121.000).
  • Insert side screen
  • Align side screen so that A-dimension is correct

Recommendation: Support cladding profile P1307 on side screens (contained in 016.121.000 or 016.141.000)

7.4 Inserting Track Support Section

  • Mark door centre with cladding profile
  • Hanging the 1- or 2-piece track support sections P1302
  • Aligning track support sections: Gap of approx. 20 mm at centre (to D-STA), left and right approx. 5 - 7mm each
  • Fixing with nuts and special screws with tongue-nut in lower oval holes (contained in 016.006.000)

7.5 Inserting Fanlight (If Provided)

  • Position connecting profile according to building situation and fit fanlight

7.6 Inserting Infill Profile P1309

  • If built-in radar is used in the cladding, provide corresponding recess (see installation instructions built-in radar)
  • Cut infill profile P1309 to length and insert in door opening with tensioning blocks (016.000.007) (contained in 016.006.000).

7.7 Horizontal Sealing Profile and Strip Brush

The horizontal sealing profile P1308 with integral strip brush P1352 is in 3 parts, with 1 part of A dimension +40 mm with slots in both pieces and at top centre for cable passage.

  • Insert strip brush P1352, likewise 3-piece, and affix lightly
  • Fit the A dimension part in the doorway (clear opening) and fix on track support profile with 2 screws
  • Cut both side pieces to length and likewise secure flush with track support profile with 2 screws

7.8 Fitting ELS

  • Fit in alu profile in the correct length
  • Fitting ELS in aluminium profile and affix
  • Draw in rubber cover profile P1339
  • Drill fixing holes (∆ 2.8mm) in cover profile P1338 (30mm) or P1337 (20mm) and side screen
  • Screw cover profile to side screen (contained in 016.141.000 or 016.121.000)

7.9 Fitting Door Leaf Guides

  • Mark position
  • Drill fixing holes
  • Fix guides

7.10 Starting Installation Without Cladding Profile (Without Side Screen)

  • Cut horizontal sealing profile P1308 to length
  • Draw in strip brush P1352 into horizontal sealing profile and affix 1 - 2 cm at both ends

Note: With a wall to wall installation the strip brush cannot be replaced later, unless the horizontal sealing profile P1308 is divided into two parts, so that 1 part can be removed again if necessary to withdraw the brush.

  • Fix horizontal sealing profile horizontally P1308 to dimension G provisionally (e.g. with screw clamp).
  • Place 1- or 2-piece track support profile P1302 on horizontal sealing profile and mark fixing holes.
  • Type of fixing depends on surface. It must be ensured that the profiles lie exactly parallel and aligned.
  • Fix horizontal sealing profile P1308 on track support profile P1302 with M6 x 12 mm screws.
  • Fix sealing profile to lintel if necessary with 2 - 3 screws.

Important: The screw heads must not project more than 8 mm.

7.11 Inserting Track Profile

  • Clean track support profile P1302
  • Clean running surface on track profile
  • Spray a little soapy water in slot if necessary
  • Insert rubber damping profile P1318
  • Spray soapy water again on rubber damping profile
  • Place 1- or 2-piece track profile P1292 on rubber damping profile P1318 and press into profile from the centre outwards
  • The rubber damping profile must still be visible at front and rear

7.12 Inserting Carriage

Specification: Max. door leaf weight 67 kg per carriage

  • Release counter wheels
  • Turn door leaf hangers right down
  • Insert carriage
  • Adjust counter wheels slightly: Place insert nut on screw of counter wheel and press firmly up with the thumbs and tighten

Title: Record 16 STA/STA-UL Automatic Door Installation Guide
Author: leo lu
Body HTML:
Installation Instructions: Record 16 STA / 16 STA-UL Automatic Door System

7.13 Setting end stops

  • Fit end stops provisionally, so that the carriages do not drop out

7.14 External radar

  • Mark radar position on outside of door with radar drilling templates and drill, or use built-in radar in cladding (see installation instructions for built-in radar)
  • Fit radar and draw in cable on inside

7.15 Hanging door leaves

  • Draw in rubber seals on door leaves and secure (drawing in is simplified by moistening the rubber seal with soapy water)
  • Hanging door leaves (if present: etched record logo must be legible from outside)
  • Connect door leaves with hangers of carriages

7.16 Adjusting door leaves

  • First set height
  • Distance behind of locking bar = 50mm (important when using a VRR). The centre buffer of the left, central carriage serves simultaneously as setting gauge.
  • All 4 carriages must be aligned
  • The door leaves must not be too close to the brush profile
  • Align door leaves slightly V-shaped
  • Tighten fixing screws (door leaf suspension with carriage) firmly
  • Tighten door leaf fixing screw (door leaf with door leaf suspension) firmly

Check counter wheels: they must not be in line and it must be possible to turn them easily!

7.17 Fixing end stops

The door can be mechanically locked from inside in this condition. For this purpose the door leaves must be closed by hand and fixed with the two end stops in this position. (Tighten only screw below)

  • Aligning and fixing end stops

7.18 Attaching drive module

  • Open door leaves approx. 400 mm
  • Attach drive module
  • Centre drive module provisionally
  • Fix slidebars, remove slidebar lock if necessary (cable ties) if they interfere with the motion
  • Centre module with door leaf exactly with respect to side screens
  • When using a lock, check engagement of locking bolts and move VRR if necessary
  • Fix module left and right with slotted angle:
    • First tighten centre screw (1) (M6 x 16)
    • Level with Allen screw (2) (M6 x 12)
    • Fix with socket-head hex. screw (3) (M6 x 10 and washer)
  • Fix lock (if provided) on track support profile P1302 with 2 additional screws M6 x 10mm and tongue nuts
  • If there is no locking device, an additional fixing will be necessary (contained in # 016.005.000)

7.19 Checking toothed belt tension

  • Check toothed belt tension and tighten if necessary:
    • Guide pulley support must be parallel to track (no distortion)
    • Tighten guide pulley support firmly

7.20 Checking door leaves by hand

  • Move door leaves by hand and check for easy running

7.21 Options

(If not already completed as preliminary work in workshop)

7.22 Cable layout

  • A slot is provided for the mains cable above the header
  • AGTA cabling below header in slot provided

7.23 Connecting electrical units

Connect BDE, ELS, radar, etc. according to chapter Cable Routing page 50 and chapter.

  • Wiring diagram page 51 and fit cable cover.
  • The power regulations must be obeyed when the BDE (factory data capture unit) is used in multiple combinations!
  • For record 16 STA-UL: Before applying the mains voltage to the power supply NET16-UL, the installer has to ensure that the mains voltage selector switch on the power supply is switched to the correct position (115V / 230V).
  • The mains power connection has to be done via the mains cord supplied with the pedestrian sliding door operator (see also schematic LS.016.001A chapter 0 page 51). Proper grounding has to be applied. Only permanent wiring is allowed with this pedestrian sliding door operator.
  • The local installation codes must always be followed.

7.24 Protection wings

  • Fit any protection wings

7.25 Final mechanical test

  • Manual door opening satisfactory over the entire opening range
  • No abnormal noises present
  • All screws tight

Title: Commissioning Guide: Record 16 STA & STA-UL Automatic Doors
Author: leo lu
Body HTML:
Commissioning and Final Work - Record 16 STA / 16 STA-UL Manual

8.1 Preparation

Safety Warning: Read safety instructions (page 4) and observe!
  • Interrupt power supply with main switch or power plug.
  • Leave door leaves open approx. 1 m.
  • Check wiring according to general schematic diagram AS.E.016.001 (page 51).

8.2 Checking Settings

  • Position jumpers for the required function.
  • Check external jumpers for auxiliary units not connected, such as EMERGENCY STOP, HEA, ELS 1, ELS 2.

8.3 Switching on Power Supply and Calibration Run

  1. Switch on power supply.
  2. A calibration run is performed automatically when switching on the supply voltage for the first time or following a hardware reset.
    Note: The door checks the weight of door leaves during braking tests.
  3. The door parameters are determined during the first 3 - 4 opening cycles.
Caution: The door must not be obstructed in any way during the calibration run.
Emergency Procedure: In the event of uncontrolled door motion, interrupt the power supply immediately, disconnect the battery, and call your service partner or installer.

8.4 Checking LEDs on the STG

Check LEDs 1, 2 and 4 - 7 according to the technical table (refer to page 38 of full manual).

8.5 Checking BDE Functions and Actuating Devices

BDE Position: Open

  • Door must open and remain open.
  • Check movement characteristics.
  • Door cannot be moved by hand when open.
  • Manual operation is obtained by pressing again; the door can then be moved freely.

BDE Position: Closed / Locked

  • Door must close.
  • Check movement characteristics.
  • Check locking if present (refer to status messages for wrong behavior).
  • Pressing initiates an SSK opening.
  • SSK must release (if present).
  • AKI and AKA must not operate.

BDE Position: One-Way

  • AKI and SSK must operate.
  • AKA must not be triggered when door is closed.

BDE Position: Automatic with Reduced Opening

  • AKI, AKA and SSK must operate.
  • Check reduced opening width.
  • Press: door opens to reduced width.

8.6 Programming Door Speeds and Hold-Open Times

These functions are described in Chapter 3rd Level (Programming Level) on page 42.

8.7 Configuration of Specific Customer Settings

The possibilities are described in application information 16.770. All modifications must be entered on the configuration sheet (situated in the operator).

8.7.1 Configuration for UL 325 Installations

In the 5th configuration level, the configuration "STA 16 UL" must be activated. For details see application information 16.770.

LED Configuration Settings (V 2.2)
Function Code (5 bits) Description
Factory setting (Default) 0 1 1 0 1 STA 16 UL not activated (LED 1=on)

8.8 Checking Safety

  • Set BDE position.
  • Open door (e.g., with AKI).
  • Cover a photocell (ELS) while closing. Door must re-open.
  • The same check must be performed if a 2nd ELS or another safety device is present.

8.9 Checking Automatic Reverse

  • Obstruct door while closing: Door must reverse. When the door next closes, it moves at creep speed past the obstruction point.
  • Obstruct the door while opening: Door stops for hold-open time and closes. When the door next opens, it moves at creep speed past the obstruction point.

8.10 Checking BAT Functions

Status 13 must be indicated on the BDE-E when removing the battery connection J7. If not indicated, jumper J13 is not at position 1 - 2 (see page 11).

8.11 Casing

With an F-dimension > 3,500 mm, 2 more multi-headers (016.007.000) must be fitted (total 4) to support the casing.

Fitting Casing

  • Divide the casing into lengths, screw together, use snap-in fastener and brush seal P1344.
  • Insert white hinge piece on casing P1341.
  • Push-in/engage casing.
  • Align casing.
  • Fit side covers if necessary.
  • Close casing and check for perfect setting.

8.12 Casing Version with Suspended Ceiling

(Refer to specific diagrams for suspended ceiling installation)

8.13 Fitting Internal Radar

  • Fit radar on casing with the aid of the drilling template or fit built-in radar.
  • Check radar settings inside and outside.

8.14 Handing Over to Customer

  • Ensure commissioning has been performed correctly according to this list.
  • The system should be handed over to the customer.
  • The functions and safety instructions must be explained with reference to the operating instructions.
  • The customer should be given a copy of the operating instructions.

Title: Record 16 STA / 16 STA-UL Operating Instructions & Manual
Author: leo lu
Body HTML:
Operating Instructions - Record 16 STA / 16 STA-UL Control Unit

9.1 Controls on STG 16

9.1.1 General

The STG 16 operates with active HIGH level, i.e., a +24 V level must be applied to activate a function. Safety inputs are activated during interruptions. The signal ground (0 V) is connected to protective earth. This connection can be removed for test purposes with the earthing screw at bottom left.

9.1.2 Jumpers

  • J11 (left): For CAN line termination (see AN1).
  • J12 (right): Direction of rotation:
    • Jumper at position 1-2 for D-STA or E-STA-R (factory setting).
    • Jumper at position 2-3 for E-STA-L.
  • J13 (top): Battery monitoring:
    • Jumper at position 1-2 for systems with battery (factory setting).
    • Jumper at position 2-3 for systems without battery.

9.1.3 LED’s (left to right)

  • LED 1 (red) Photocell 1: Lights when obstruction present.
  • LED 2 (red) Photocell 2: Lights when obstruction present.
  • LED 3 (red) Ground: Must light when earthing screw removed (bottom left). Otherwise an earth connection is present.
  • LED 4 (red) Limit switch: Lights up when limit switch is closed.
  • LED 5 (green) +24V: Lights when mains or battery voltage present.
    Caution: In the event of a power failure, processor reset only takes place 1 sec. after this LED extinguishes.
  • LED 6 (green) +35 V: Off for power failure.
  • LED 7 (red): Large control LED right for push-button operation.

9.1.4 Key

This multifunction key has several functions. The selection of function is made with the aid of the neighbouring control LED according to the following table.

Release key while: Function
1st light pulse on LED 7 AKI
2nd light pulse on LED 7 Learn ELS
3rd light pulse on LED 7 Learn door parameters
4th light pulse on LED 7 Configuration mode on
5th light pulse on LED 7 BAT emergency reaction if no mains present
6th light pulse on LED 7 Factory setting for redundancy module
8th light pulse on LED 7 Factory setting of programming and configurations
Press key approx. 13 seconds Hardware reset (new control start)

9.2 Functions of electronic BDE-E

9.2.1 General

The electronic control unit BDE-E is a convenient input and output unit. It contains several virtual control levels. The normal level (1st level) contains the standard modes of operation.

All LED’s light in sequence during the first few seconds after switching on the power supply (run light) and the last operating mode is then displayed.

9.2.2 1st level (operating modes)

9.2.3 Key functions

  • One-way operation
  • Winter mode
  • Automatic mode
  • Continuously open
  • Locked

Programming:

  • Programming decrement
  • Programming increment

A LED indication is assigned to every key, with the exception of the two keys for programming. The LED is off in this level.

  • If the key is pressed again in the „locked“ status, an SSK opening takes place.
  • If the key is pressed again in the „continuously open“ status, manual operation takes place.
  • If the key is pressed for approx. 5 secs. the control is restarted. The programmed data remain stored.

9.2.4 2nd level (control lock)

Entry to this level with key sequence:

The LED lights. The BDE is blocked.

Exit from this level with key sequence:

This releases operation again.

9.2.5 3rd level (programming level)

Entry to this level with key sequence:

  • The LED flashes slowly
  • Selection of following menus by key operation
  • The value is displayed while the key remains pressed

The value display takes place proportionately in max. 40 increments. Divided in 5 LED’s from left to right, with each LED divided into 8 increments. The range from 0% to 100% is thereby covered.

Example: 75% winter opening
  • LED’s fully lit (corresponding to 3 times 8 increments)
  • LED has an on/off ratio of 6/2 (corresponding to 6 increments)
  • LED remains off. Therefore total 30 increments, i.e. 75%.

Menu functions

Function Range Step width Factory setting
Closing speed 3 - 50 cm/s 1,25 cm/s 40 cm/s
Winter opening width * 20 cm - 100% approx. 1 cm steps 62,5%
Door hold-open time 0 - 20 s 0,5 s 1 s
Door hold-open time SSK 0 - 20 s 0,5 s 10 s
Opening speed 3 - 70 cm/s 1,75 cm/s 50 cm/s

* on „continuously open“ the door follows the ONLINE winter opening width

Setting

  • Following menu selection (the LED of the menu selected lights) the value can be changed by pressing the keys several times.
  • The current value is continuously displayed while this key is pressed.
  • At the highest range limit the setting returns to the lowest value and vice-versa.
  • The value is reset to the factory setting by pressing the keys simultaneously.
  • Exit from this level is made by pressing the key briefly or if no operation is made for 3 minutes.

9.3 Functions of mechanical BDE-M

9.3.1 General

The mechanical control unit BDE-M is a simple input unit with a key switch. The key can be withdrawn at any position. Winter operation is possible if required.

9.3.2 Modes of operation

  • One-way operation (or winter)
  • Automatic mode
  • Continuously open
  • Locked

Operating indication

The LED lights when mains or battery voltage is present.

9.3.3 Reset key

This hidden key is operated with a paper clip approx. 25 mm long. A small hole is provided for this purpose at the centre of the record logo.

If this key is pressed for approx. 5 seconds, the control unit starts completely new. The programmed data remain stored.

Title: Record STA 16 Fault Signals & Status Codes
Author: leo lu
Body HTML:
Record BDE-D Programmer

In the event of an irregularity on your Record STA 16 system, the system automatically switches from the operating mode level to the status level. Change is made approx. every 5 seconds between status and operating mode level. No status display is given in the remaining levels.

Characteristic of the status level are 2 or more rapidly flashing LEDs (of 6 total). This permits a maximum of 58 different status numbers to be output. A status with "W" is a warning, which is not followed by switching of the fault output relay.

LED Status Codes (BDE-E)

Overview of LED patterns and Status Codes
LEDs Active Status Details
1 2 3 4 5 6 Code & Description

04W Manual operation
05 AKA sensor active > 60s

09 Battery fuse blown
10 Locking error; door not closed
12 Battery defective (voltage too low)
14 Locking n/o contact defective
20* Door leaf interception error

Author: leo lu
Body HTML:
ASSA ABLOY SL500 Safety Instructions & Operation Manual

Instructions for Safe Operation

Important Safety Notice: Failure to observe the information in this manual may result in personal injury or damage to equipment.
  • To reduce the risk of injury of persons - use this operator only with pedestrian doors.
  • Do not use the equipment if repair or adjustment is necessary.
  • Disconnect supply when cleaning or other maintenance is to be carried out.
  • The operator can be used by children age 8 and above, and persons with reduced physical, sensory or mental capabilities, or lack of experience and knowledge, if they have been given supervision or instruction by a person responsible for their safety concerning safe operator use and the possible hazards involved. This does not however prevent those persons to use the door where the operator is installed.
  • Cleaning and user maintenance shall not be made by children without supervision.
  • Do not let children climb on or play with the door or the fixed/remote controls.
  • Installer must properly ground door package! Improper grounding can lead to risk of personal injury.
  • The doorset can be operated automatically by sensors or manually by activators.

Introduction

Congratulations on your new automatic door! ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems has developed automatic doors for more than 50 years. State-of-the-art technology and carefully tested materials and components provide you with a superior product.

As with all other technical products, your automatic door requires periodic maintenance and service. It is essential that you know your automatic door (system) and that you recognize the importance of maintaining it in compliance with applicable standards for safety.

Your local ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems-authorized representative is familiar with these standards, as well as all applicable local codes and ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems recommendations for power-operated pedestrian doors. Service and adjustments performed by your ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems-authorized representative will ensure safe and proper operation of your automatic door unit.

Electronic Equipment Reception Interference

The equipment complies with the European EMC directive (US market FCC Part 15), provided installed according to Installation and Service manual.

The equipment may generate and use radio frequency energy and if not installed and used properly, it may cause interference to radio, television reception or other radio frequency type systems.

If other equipment does not fully comply with immunity requirements interference may occur. There is no guarantee that interference will not occur in a particular installation. If this equipment does cause interference to radio or television reception, which can be determined by turning the equipment off and on, the user is encouraged to try to correct the interference by one or more of the following measures:

  • Re-orient the receiving antenna.
  • Relocate the receiver with respect to the equipment.
  • Move the receiver away from the equipment.
  • Plug the receiver into a different outlet so that equipment and receiver are on different branch circuits.
  • Check that protective earth (PE) is connected.

If necessary, the user should consult the dealer or an experienced electronics technician for additional suggestions.

Environmental Requirements

ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems products are equipped with electronics and may also be equipped with batteries containing materials which are hazardous to the environment. Disconnect power before removing electronics and battery and make sure it is disposed of properly according to local regulations (how and where) as was done with the packaging material.

Product Liability

According to regulations, the following are the responsibility of the owner or caretaker of the equipment:

  • That the equipment operates correctly, so that it gives sufficient protection in regard to safety and health.
  • That the equipment is operated and regularly maintained, inspected, and serviced by someone with documented competence in the equipment and in applicable regulations.
  • That the provided “Service Log Book” and “Site Acceptance Test and Risk Assessment” documents (PRA-0005) are kept available for maintenance and service records.
  • That inspection covers the emergency opening function (when applicable).
  • That the closing force is appropriate for the door size on fire-approved door systems (when applicable).

ASSA ABLOY SL500 Series - User Manual & Warranty Information

Warranty

ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems warrants its products to be free from defects in material and workmanship under intended use and service for a warranty time of 12 months, beginning at time of delivery. This warranty extends only to the original buyer of the equipment.

ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems warrants that the software will operate substantially in accordance with its functional descriptions and that it has been recorded on non-defective media.

Warranty Exclusions

The ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems warranty does not apply to:

  • Software to be error-free or operate without interruption
  • General wear and tear on the system
  • Fuse, disposable batteries, and glass damage
  • System deviations caused by installers other than ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems
  • System that has been altered or damaged by vandalism or misuse
  • System that has been additionally equipped with non-ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems original branded parts and/or spare parts
  • Unrequired visits due to poor client communication (e.g., door working when our technician arrives, reset, power discontinuation)
  • Adjustments (closing and opening speed and also detection field radars) due to customer requests (excludes operational adjustments thought to create a hazard)
  • Water damage

  • Any damage caused, directly or indirectly, by a circumstance beyond the control of the applicable company within ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems, such as industrial dispute, fire, natural disaster, war, extensive military mobilization, insurrection, requisition, seizure, embargo, restrictions in the use of power, and defects or delays in deliveries by sub-contractors caused by any such circumstances.
Please note:
  • Non-compliance with manufacturer's care and maintenance recommendations may void the warranty.
  • ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems authorized resellers shall extend this warranty to end-users only, but have no authority to extend a greater or different warranty on behalf of ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems.
  • A service agreement with ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems will help secure the availability of a fully operational system and will give priority at call-out, thus minimizing the time that the equipment is unusable.

Service

Regular inspections by a trained and qualified person, and the frequency of service occasions, should at minimum be made according to national regulations or industry standard, in the absence of a national regulation.

This is especially important when the installation concerns a fire-approved door or a door with an emergency-opening function.

To extend the life of your investment and ensure safe and reliable operation of the door, we recommend a minimum of 2 visits per year or more, depending on usage and operating conditions. Environmental aspects shall also be considered.

As your entrances are part of your business flow, there’s every reason to keep them working well. ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems offers you maintenance and modernization expertise to rely on. Our Maintenance Programs and Modernization Services for entrance automation are backed by extensive expertise for all types of pedestrian and industrial door and docking systems, independent of brand.

At your disposal is a team of dedicated expert technicians, proven through decades of maintenance, service, and satisfied customers.

Intended Use

The Besam SL 500, Besam SL500 T, and Besam SL500 SL are automatic sliding door operators developed to facilitate entrances to buildings and within buildings through sliding doors.

The door is designed to offer continuous use, a high degree of safety, and maximum lifetime. The system is self-adjusting to the effects caused by normal variations in the weather conditions and to minor friction changes caused by e.g. dust and dirt.

Emergency Functions

In emergency situations, the doorset is opened and remains open automatically. It may also be equipped with a break-out function, in which case the door leaf is pushed manually open in the escape direction.

Dual batteries and motors are used in escape routes as indicated in associated certificates. (See "Electrical emergency unit with batteries" and "Electrical emergency unit with batteries and two motors" in the full manual). For manual break-out, see "Break-out unit PSB".

It is to be used indoors where it is suitable for almost all types of external and internal SL500 sliding door configurations.

Safety Note: Ensure that the lock is only activated when there are no persons in the room.

Technical Specifications

Information regarding the Besam SL500 Series
Manufacturer ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems AB
Address Lodjursgatan 10, SE-261 44 Landskrona, Sweden
Type Sliding Door Operator Besam SL500, Besam SL500 T, and Besam SL500 SL
Mains Power Supply 100 V AC -10% to 240 V AC +10%, 50/60 Hz, fuse 10 AT
Power Consumption Max. 250 W
Degree of Protection IP20
Approvals Third party approvals from established certification organizations valid for safety in use, see Declaration of Conformity.

How It Works

The Besam SL500 sliding automatic doors, including the Besam SL500 T and Besam SL500 SL models, work electromechanically.

The motor, control unit, transmission – and optional emergency unit and electromechanical locking device – are all assembled in a support beam with an integrated cover.

  • The motor and gear box transmit movement to the door leaves by means of a tooth belt.
  • The door leaf is fitted to a door adapter/carriage wheel fitting and hangs on a sliding track.
  • The guiding at the bottom is carried out by means of floor guides (Full Break-Out) or Side Panel Guides (Fixed Sidelites).

Operation Cycle:

  1. When an OPENING IMPULSE is received by the control unit, the motor starts and transmits movement to the door leaves, which move to the open position.
  2. The closing starts when no OPENING IMPULSE is received and the HOLD OPEN TIME has expired.

The user can select five different modes of operation if a programme selector is installed.

Locking & Unlocking

Locking

Doors used for emergency escape in buildings such as hospitals and homes for elderly people may not be locked or put in programme selection OFF mode. In other buildings, emergency escape doors may be locked or put in programme selection OFF mode after it has been secured and all people have left the building.

Unlocking

Unlock all the mechanical locks before activating the operator.

Body HTML:
Program selector PS-6
ASSA ABLOY SL500 Operation Mode Selector - User Manual & Functions

Operation Mode Selectors

The door functions of the SL500 are set with different operate mode selectors. The operation mode selector is available with 5 buttons (plus RESET).

Safety Note: The key on the PSK-6U mode selector must always be removed on emergency escape doors after changing settings.

If monitored emergency unit is a demand, a test of the emergency unit is performed when the operate mode selector is set from OFF or OPEN to any other operation mode.

Functions

The following operating functions can be obtained: OPEN, AUTO PARTIAL, AUTO, ONE WAY, and OFF.

OPEN

The door is permanently open. The door can be moved by hand (e.g., for window cleaning). All activation units except for the emergency push button (if fitted) are disconnected.

AUTO PARTIAL

Two-way traffic, AUTO PARTIAL is obtained. The door can be opened partially with the inner and outer activation units and with a key switch (if fitted). With an emergency push-button, the door opens fully.

AUTO

Two-way traffic, normal operation of the door. The door can be opened with the inner and outer activation units and with a key switch/emergency push-button (if fitted).

ONE WAY

Passage from inside only. The door is normally locked if an electromechanical locking device has been fitted. The door can only be opened with the inner activation unit or with a key switch/emergency push-button (if fitted).

OFF

This function is only used on emergency escape doors after it is certain that all people have left the building. Features include:

  • The door cannot be opened with inner and outer activation units.
  • The door is locked if an electromechanical locking device has been fitted.
  • The door can be opened partially with a key switch (if fitted).
  • With an emergency pushbutton (if fitted) the door opens fully.
  • The door can also be opened partially from the operation mode selector if the arrow down button is held for 2 seconds. No access code is necessary for this, and the key impulse is indicated by briefly showing a blue light to the left of the open symbol or text and then a flashing blue light to the left of the closed symbol or text for another 15 seconds.

Reset Instructions

Standard Reset

By briefly pushing the globe of the logotype with a narrow object, the door operator will make a RESET function with a system test. The door will return to the closed position (if not in operation mode selection OPEN or if an error is present) and is then ready for normal operation.

PSK-6U Key Reset

Turn the key clockwise to the position “R” (six o’clock) and insert a narrow object in the small hole on the operation mode selector and push briefly. Then turn the key counter-clockwise back to the requested setting and the door operator will make a RESET function with a system test. The door will return to the closed position (if not in operation mode selection OPEN or if an error is present) and is then ready for normal operation.

Note: The key cannot be removed in the "R" position.

Access Codes and Selection

The different operation modes are selected by pushing the arrow symbols pointing upwards (Up) or downwards (Down). When a button is pushed a buzzer will sound. The present selection is indicated by a blue light to the left of the function symbol or text.

When an arrow symbol has not been pushed for 15 seconds the access will be locked.

Selectable Codes

Three alternative selectable codes are used:

  1. Default Access: Obtained by pushing the arrow symbol pointing up or down for 2 seconds.
  2. Optional Access Code: Access is obtained by briefly pushing in turn:
    • Arrow UP symbol
    • Arrow DOWN symbol
    • Arrow DOWN symbol again
    • Arrow UP symbol (last)
    The entire code must be entered within 3 seconds.
  3. No Access Code: Direct selection.

Flashing Light Indicators (Troubleshooting)

Red Light

Every other second: Indicates an error in the door operator. If the error remains after a RESET then service is needed for your assa abloy door lock.

Quickly flashing (3/sec): Indicates an internal error in the operation mode selector.

Orange Light

Every other second: Indicates a status or condition that can be cleared by the owner (e.g., a break-out door is standing open).

Yellow Light

Every other second: Indicates that maintenance is needed.

Integrated Safety

To permit a safe passage between closing doors, the doors reverse immediately if an obstruction is detected. They then resume their interrupted movement at low speed to check whether the obstruction has disappeared or not.

If an obstruction is detected between opening doors and surrounding walls or interior fittings, the doors stop immediately, and then close after a time delay.
